Index: docs/kit/02-api-reference.md
===================================================================
--- docs/kit/02-api-reference.md
+++ docs/kit/02-api-reference.md
@@ -152,8 +152,10 @@
 
 Statistics exposures and credits require an explicit valid slot configuration (missing/invalid:400). A changed reward, objective (absent means `unit`) or `tauLearnMs` refuses with409 and `applied:false` before either item or slot counters, storage or alarms change. Estimator-only `n0`, `nMin` and lift clamps remain editable without discarding counts. Current outcome producers explicitly carry the resolved document's default configuration for unconfigured slots; the ring never infers one from stored history or silently replaces a malformed override. New snapshots publish `tauLearnMs`; live serving checks owner, reward, objective, horizon and estimator settings on fresh reads and cache hits. Missing legacy horizon or mismatch omits learned evidence without erasing the cached snapshot or overriding an explicit operator-frozen lift. Archived pure replay is unchanged. This is forward containment, not proof of clean legacy history, atomic configuration rollout, reward filtering, reset/rebuild, generation transition or money/attribution-policy reconciliation; old binaries and historical aggregates remain separate work.
 
-The upgraded statistics publisher freezes estimates/time, creates the R2 archive without overwriting a retained key, validates its acknowledgement, then awaits live KV publication. Same-millisecond/reset/restart collisions try at most eight positive safe-integer versions; only a definite collision advances, while missing, failed or malformed acknowledgements stop. Final serialized bytes remain within the snapshot budget. Publication failure schedules another attempt in30 seconds and still fails; scheduling failure also fails. State/prior/snapshot refusals retain their existing behavior. Operator publish/reset requires coherent downstream success; failures return503 and reset does not append a successful revision. KV or item-reset may already have committed, so failure is not rollback. Ambiguous archive writes may leave orphan versions. This is not a page-wide manifest, coupled-slot/exploration/gamma-zero replay fix, dependency-aware pin repair, globally chronological/idempotent version identity, retention/history repair or mixed-version rollout guarantee. Old unconditional publishers and externally removed/corrupt archives remain separate work; no extra decision hot-path read is added.
+The upgraded statistics publisher freezes estimates/time, creates the R2 archive without overwriting a retained key, validates its acknowledgement, then awaits live KV publication. Same-millisecond/reset/restart collisions try at most eight positive safe-integer versions; only a definite collision advances, while missing, failed or malformed acknowledgements stop. Final serialized bytes remain within the snapshot budget. Publication failure schedules another attempt in30 seconds and still fails; scheduling failure also fails. State/prior/snapshot refusals retain their existing behavior. Operator publish/reset requires coherent downstream success; failures return503 and reset does not append a successful revision. KV or item-reset may already have committed, so failure is not rollback. Ambiguous archive writes may leave orphan versions. This does not establish globally chronological/idempotent version identity, retention/history repair or mixed-version rollout. Old unconditional publishers and externally removed/corrupt archives remain separate work; no extra decision hot-path read is added.
 
+New decision inputs include `replay: {version:1, learning, candidateLimit, slots:[{slot,lift,prior}]}`: the ordered full page's effective learning presence, candidate limit and snapshot identities. Pins/default-arm slots name zero dependencies. Replay validates this manifest and required archive owner/version/prior/consumed structure, then runs the ranked prefix through the target; a genuine catalog pin runs alone without unused archives. Gamma zero still requires any snapshots used for raw receipts or exploration. Returned records retain detached full-page inputs; `used.lift/prior` describes the consumed target snapshot, while the manifest can name later archives that were not read. Comparison includes authority and exploration metadata. Absent legacy personalized multi-slot manifests refuse; default/pin and qualified single-slot compatibility cannot recover arbitrary old pure-call candidate limits or ambiguous zero-lift exploration/controls. Present malformed manifests never become legacy fallback. Repeated page metadata counts toward existing full-record queue budgets. This is deterministic forward replay, not cryptographic receipt integrity, repaired archives, complete retention/rollout/resource assurance or statistical validation of Thompson exploration.
+
 Snapshots contain only their named identity fields and estimates, not raw statistics/configuration. Prior documents are gated at4096 rows/256KiB before indexing/building; selected keys allow at most six components/2048 bytes, and actual item/key/ancestor expansion shares the256-item/4096-counter limits. Output is capped at2MiB before response/publication. This gate follows the existing configuration read/validation, so it is not a bound on raw KV parsing/import allocation. These are application budgets tested with synthetic bounded storage, not native provider-limit or sustained-capacity proof. Historical oversized-object reconstruction, old KV snapshots/completeness policy, vocabulary/estimator/generation policy and full W10 remain separate work.
 
 Imported priors now preserve item and cell as separate identities through duplicate detection, lookup, publication and capacity counting. Multi-component cells materialize under the real item at each current ladder level; a finer prior overrides its ancestor. Raw snapshot/decision `n` and `s` remain observed counts, while `n0`, `prior: {p,n}` and the prior revision identify imported strength. A cold item can therefore receive a prior-derived ranking term in an eventful slot with positive reference and base scores. The prior document and snapshot formats are unchanged, but old readers can reject newly accepted delimiter-collision pairs. This does not repair old snapshots, publish event-free slots, version/validate the complete cell grammar, resolve money or zero-reference/base semantics, or correct human-readable receipt prose. Prior strength is not observed exposure or causal lift.
@@ -253,7 +255,7 @@
 | `GET ledger/batches?date=YYYY-MM-DD[&stream=decision\|outcome\|product-sort][&cursor=]` | The day's batch objects, so a warehouse job knows what to fetch with its own storage credentials. Product-sort objects require the explicit selector; apply erasure cutoffs when loading |
 | `GET ledger/erasures` | The visitors whose erasure is pending, each with the moment of erasure: a warehouse job drops their rows at or before that moment from what it loads, until the nightly rewrite has removed them from the objects themselves. `ledger/batches` says how many are pending |
 | `POST ledger/erasures` `{ visitorId }` | The ledger half of an erasure: writes the tombstone every reader honours at once and empties the visitor's ring. The identity erase route calls the same function after erasing the profile. `POST ledger/erasures/rewrite` runs the nightly rewrite now |
-| `GET replay/{decision_id}` | Decides again from the documents at the recorded revisions, the archived snapshot and the record's inputs, and compares field by field: `{ equal, diff[], used }` |
+| `GET replay/{decision_id}` | Validates recorded page dependencies, loads required prefix archives (none for a genuine pin), and compares the target including authority/exploration: `{ equal, diff[], used }`; unavailable or inconsistent dependencies fail explicitly |
 | `POST learn/report` `{ date, brand?, policies? }` and `GET learn/report?date=&brand=` | The day under the learning policy and the reporting overlays side by side, the holdout arms, the realized exploration share. The day is the sum of its hours: five minutes after an hour closes the platform folds its ledger objects into one aggregate, so a day of any size answers, and `GET` for today answers through the last closed hour. `hours` says which hours are in (`built`), which closed hours are not yet (`missing`), and how far back the batch ring reaches when it credits an outcome (`horizonMs`, two days). Custom `policies` are computed over the records themselves and answer 413 past 800 ledger objects in the day; the built-in overlays never do. No visitor id in the result |
 | `POST learn/cycle[?brand=]` | Unavailable: valid authenticated requests return 503. Automatic and on-demand proposal generation/application are withdrawn pending W29 safeguards |
 | `GET learn/proposals` | Read-only historical records, explicitly unverified; retained statuses are not proof of successful application and the returned history is not guaranteed complete |
